decision: Substitutions/absences as a thin declaration+routing layer over already-ratified primitives, no new authority subsystem. (1) New tenant-isolated table substitution_rule (migration 036) declaring who substitutes for whom over which role_id and org_scope across [valid_from,valid_until), with the role_assignment proposal/confirmation contract (confirmed_by NULL=proposal/zero-capability, NOT NULL=effective), T-0013 invariants (tenant_id leading PK, FORCE RLS, default-DENY policy, choros_app DML-only), composite tenant-scoped FKs to employee (both sides), role, and grant (ttl_grant_id), two CHECKs (no-self-substitution, window sanity), and an idempotent dev seed (a-recon substitutes e-mironov under budget-approver in fin dept, Tier-1, confirmed_by='seed'). (2) Two tiers: Tier-1 default = routing-layer stand-in, ttl_grant_id NULL, NO grant minted, stand-in uses own role authority; Tier-2 fallback = TTL'd grant minted by the future write-API with valid_until=TTL, valid_from=now, delegable=false, granted_by='substitution:<rule_id>', id recorded in substitution_rule.ttl_grant_id. (3) grant table gets NO new column: TTL rides existing grant.valid_until + isEffective (expiry needs zero gateway code, resolveFor already denies 'no_grant' past valid_until); provenance rides existing granted_by; both NF-4 escape hatches (TTL column, source column) are REJECTED to keep grant frozen. (4) Non-inheritable exclusion is a grant.constraint jsonb convention {non_inheritable:true}, exported as pure isNonInheritable(grant) + eligibleForTier2 filter for the mint site. (5) New pure module src/core/substitution.ts holds SubstitutionRule type, SubstitutionSource port (getActiveSubstitutions, getSubstitutionForSubstitute), resolveSubstitution pure selector reusing isNarrowerOrEqual over hierarchy 'org', isEffectiveWindow/isRuleEffective, and an in-memory test source; Postgres-backed port deferred to T-0053. (6) grant-resolver.ts touched additively ONLY by one optional ResolverDeps property substitution?: SubstitutionSource (wired for the future routing layer, NOT consulted inside resolveFor, so the PDP keeps deciding on T-0018 grant rows only); resolveFor byte-stable when absent. (7) on_behalf_of threading reuses existing GuardContext.onBehalfOf (T-0032) -> actor_event.on_behalf_of (T-0019), actor=substituteEmployeeId / onBehalfOf=absentEmployeeId, SoD attributes COALESCE(on_behalf_of,actor); NO new GuardContext/actor_event field. (8) substitution_rule added to known_tenant_tables.txt so the table-agnostic cross_tenant.test.ts/schema.test.ts sweep it with no test-source edit; new ci/checks/substitution-isolation.sh appended to npm run fitness. Runtime target: pure static-now TS core (no DB/IO/LLM), migration 036 under choros_migrator, read path under choros_app within withTenant; no new process or dependency.

rejected_alternatives.option: New valid_until_ttl / is_substitution column on grant for the TTL
rejected_alternatives.why_not: NF-4 forbids a TTL column; grant.valid_until + isEffective ARE the TTL already. Touching the frozen, parallel-edited 008_grant.sql widens collision risk for zero gain.

rejected_alternatives.option: New source text column on grant (the NF-4 escape hatch) to mark substitution provenance
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Permitted by spec but unnecessary: granted_by='substitution:<rule_id>' identifies provenance without a schema change. Keeping grant frozen is the smaller, safer kernel (proportionality).

rejected_alternatives.option: Consult SubstitutionSource inside resolveFor to auto-resolve a stand-in at decision time
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Routing-engine reassignment is orchestrator-layer and explicitly out of scope; it would re-introduce a decision-time fork into the PDP, breaking the T-0021 grant-rows-only / single-projection invariant. The port is wired but unconsulted; a Tier-2 grant is just a grant to the PDP.

rejected_alternatives.option: New substitution scope hierarchy or new lattice element kind
rejected_alternatives.why_not: No new algebra needed: org-scope containment is the existing isNarrowerOrEqual over hierarchy 'org' with the injected AncestryOracle.

rejected_alternatives.option: Enforce confirmed_by / validity window via DB CHECK
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Mirrors role_assignment (T-0022): proposal/confirmation + window semantics are enforced at the resolution boundary (port query / pure function), not a CHECK. DB enforces NOT NULL + valid jsonb + the two structural CHECKs only.

rejected_alternatives.option: New actor_event column to mark a substituted action
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The existing actor != on_behalf_of pair already encodes it; detail can carry the rule id if needed. actor-event.ts stays a frozen file.

fields.name: org_scope
fields.type: jsonb NOT NULL (ScopeElement hierarchy 'org'; structural validation app-layer)

fields.name: CHECK substitution_rule_window_sane
fields.type: CHECK (valid_from IS NULL OR valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from < valid_until)

fields.name: RLS
fields.type: ENABLE+FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; policy USING/WITH CHECK (tenant_id=current_setting('choros.tenant_id',true)::uuid); GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE TO choros_app

fields.name: getActiveSubstitutions

fields.name: getSubstitutionForSubstitute
fields.type: (tenantId: string, substituteEmployeeId: string, absentEmployeeId: string, roleId: string, nowMs: number) => Promise<SubstitutionRule | null>

fields.name: isEffectiveWindow
fields.type: (validFrom: number|null, validUntil: number|null, nowMs: number) => boolean

fields.name: resolveSubstitution
fields.type: (rules: SubstitutionRule[], employeeId: string, roleId: string, orgScope: ScopeElement, ancestry: AncestryOracle, nowMs: number) => SubstitutionRule | null

fields.name: eligibleForTier2
fields.type: (rule: SubstitutionRule, roleGrants: Grant[]) => Grant[] (drops non-inheritable when rule.nonInheritableExcluded)

C-2 T-0044: a Tier-2 TTL'd grant expanding a criticality-(a/b/c) capability fires the T-0044 dual-control gate at grant-mint; T-0035 documents the invariant, does not implement the gate.

C-3 T-0019/T-0021: substitute action => GuardContext{actor:substituteEmployeeId, onBehalfOf:absentEmployeeId}; actor_event row carries both distinct; SoD attributes COALESCE(on_behalf_of,actor); existing fields only.
C-4 routing layer (future): consults getActiveSubstitutions; ttl_grant_id NULL => Tier-1 (stand-in uses own role, no mint); ttl_grant_id NOT NULL => Tier-2 grant already live.

C-5 Tier-2 mint site (future write-API): uses eligibleForTier2(rule,roleGrants)+isNonInheritable; mints grant with delegable=false, valid_until=TTL, granted_by='substitution:<rule_id>'; writes new grant id to substitution_rule.ttl_grant_id; no new grant column.
